newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cyprus talks to be held in upstate New York.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus talks to be held in upstate New York.

text.p: Talks next month between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities will take place at a rural resort called Troutbeck, about 90 miles 145 km north of New York, a U.N. spokesman said on Wednesday.
Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides, as head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are to hold previously announced meetings from July 9 to 13.
The aim is to revive dormant negotiations aimed at reuniting the divided island under a bi-zonal, bi-communal federal system.
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when troops from Turkey took over the north of the island after a coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece.
U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard told reporters that Secretary-General Kofi Annan would deliver an opening statement, which would be open to the press.
The talks themselves are expected to be kept under tight wraps.
Eckhard said a document had been presented to the two sides, but declined to give details.
